name: Data Cleaning & Wrangling
description: Detecting and fixing missing, duplicate, inconsistent and mistyped data, and reshaping it into analysis-ready form with pandas.

questions.question: Which pandas method returns a boolean mask showing where values are missing?
questions.explanation: isna() (alias isnull()) marks missing values as True. dropna removes them and fillna replaces them.

questions.question: What does df.drop_duplicates() do by default?
options: Removes rows that contain any missing value
Sorts the DataFrame by its index
Removes rows that are exact duplicates of an earlier row across all columns, keeping the first
questions.explanation: By default drop_duplicates compares all columns and keeps the first occurrence (keep='first').

questions.question: A 'price' column contains strings like "1,200" and "N/A". Which code converts it to numbers, turning unparseable values into NaN?
questions.explanation: Removing thousands separators then using to_numeric with errors='coerce' converts valid numbers and sets invalid ones to NaN; astype(int) would raise an error.

questions.question: Why is median imputation often preferred over mean imputation for a heavily right-skewed income column?
options: The median is less influenced by extreme values, so imputed values are more typical
The median is always zero for skewed data
Mean imputation is not supported in pandas
The median removes outliers from the data set
questions.explanation: In skewed data a few large values inflate the mean; the median better represents a typical observation.

questions.question: A table has columns id, sales_2022, sales_2023, sales_2024. Which pandas operation reshapes it into a long format with columns id, year and sales?
questions.explanation: melt unpivots wide columns into variable/value pairs (wide to long). pivot does the reverse.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to set 'status' to 'inactive' for rows where 'last_login' is before 2023, avoiding chained-assignment problems?
questions.explanation: .loc with a row mask and column label assigns in a single step on the original DataFrame; chained indexing may modify a copy.

practical.title: Clean a customer table with pandas
practical.instructions: A pandas DataFrame df has columns 'email' and 'age'. Write pandas code that (1) strips surrounding whitespace and lowercases the emails, (2) removes duplicate rows based on email, and (3) fills missing ages with the median age.
practical.expected_output: df['email'] = df['email'].str.strip().str.lower(); df = df.drop_duplicates(subset='email'); df['age'] = df['age'].fillna(df['age'].median())

rubric.hint: Use drop_duplicates(subset='email') so duplicates are judged by email.

rubric.description: Fills missing ages with the median
